about: The defect classes of the accessibility skill, for scripts: references/classes.md is the same table for a reader, row for row. Every cluster of tests/a11y/issues.json names one class in defectClass. A class has id, name, wcag (WCAG 2.2 criteria), home (where its rule text lives: skill, docs, website, or record-only for a class no rule can prevent), rule (null for record-only), enforcedBy (check: an id of EVIDENCE_CHECKS or SITE_CHECKS in tests/lib, axe, docs-axe, website-axe, unit, e2e, readers, or none; runs: pull-request (it reports on the pull request; knownChecks() says which checks do), weekly or none; an optional note) and strikes (a finding of the weekly audit that broke the rule: { cluster, audit, pullRequest }). notPreventable lists the clusters no rule can prevent, as { cluster, reason }. budget caps SKILL.md. scripts/__tests__/a11y-skill-rules.test.mjs enforces all of it.

classes.name: One grid tree: overlay copies and the rendered band
classes.rule: The grid keeps `role`, `aria-rowcount`, `aria-colcount`, `aria-rowindex`, `aria-colindex` and `aria-selected` through a change to rendering, selection, headers, frozen areas or merged cells. A layer that repeats cells, headers or rows says which copy assistive technology reads and hides the others, and a change to the rendered structure updates the tree golden in the same pull request.

classes.name: Widget role without its required structure
classes.rule: Every role has the parents and children the ARIA spec requires, with `presentation` on the table markup in between, one role per interactive element, and states only on roles that support them. `combobox` never goes on a `textarea`.

enforcedBy.note: the only run of aria-allowed-role, the rule that refuses a combobox on a textarea

classes.name: Control or focus stop with no name or role
classes.rule: Every control has a name from an i18n phrase that contains its visible text, and anything that takes focus has a role and a name. A message that needs no focus is a live region, never a tab stop.

classes.name: Focus not returned, or a tab stop that should not exist
classes.rule: Closing a surface by Escape, Enter, Tab or a shortcut returns focus to the cell or the opener. Closed or hidden UI holds no tab stop: `hidden` or `inert`, never `aria-hidden` alone.

classes.name: Focus taken or context changed without a request
classes.rule: Only the user moves focus: `updateSettings()`, `render()` and enabling or disabling a plugin call `focus()` only if the grid held the focus when the call began. Focus arriving on a control changes no context.

enforcedBy.note: the docs examples are the only pages that change a setting while a control outside the grid holds the focus
a change of context on focus or on input; no catalog page updates settings

classes.name: Keyboard trap or keyboard-only gap
classes.rule: Every pointer action has a keyboard path through a shortcut context. Tab can leave every surface Tab can enter, and only a modal dialog holds the focus. A shortcut of one character with no modifier works only while its surface has the focus.

classes.name: Focus indicator missing or hidden
classes.rule: An outline is never removed without a replacement at 3:1, a control hidden until hover also shows on `:focus-visible`, and no sticky bar or overlay fully hides the focused element.

enforcedBy.note: a control shown only on hover

classes.name: Theme tokens: contrast and target size
classes.rule: Colors and sizes come from theme tokens, and every pair clears its ratio in `main`, `horizon` and `classic`, light and dark: text 4.5:1, icons, borders and focus rings 3:1, pointer targets 24 by 24 CSS pixels.

classes.name: Pointer: action on press, drag with no other way
classes.rule: A control acts on release, never on press. A press that starts a drag or a selection is the exception, and every drag also has a single-pointer way that needs no dragging.

classes.name: Reflow, zoom, text spacing, hover content and motion
classes.rule: Surfaces around the grid reflow at 320 CSS px and 200% zoom with no sideways scroll and no clipped text, and survive the text-spacing overrides. Hover and focus content can be dismissed and hovered, nothing moves on its own for more than five seconds without a way to stop it, and, as a house rule beyond the AA bar, motion stops under the reduced-motion preference.

classes.name: Color alone: a state, an indicator or a link
classes.rule: A state a color draws (current, selected, highlighted, focused) also draws a border, an outline or text, so it survives `forced-colors: active`, and a link in text is underlined, never told apart by its color alone.

classes.name: Change not announced
classes.rule: A change without a focus move is announced through `announce()`, politely unless it is an error, once per user action. A live region is in the DOM before its text changes, and hidden status text is its own element, apart from the value.

enforcedBy.note: the flow that reads the live region, written per change

classes.name: State or annotation not exposed
classes.rule: A state a class draws (invalid, read only, commented, merged, a link or a formula in a cell) is also an ARIA attribute or hidden text a screen reader gets. A slider or splitter has `aria-valuetext` in words, from an i18n phrase.

classes.name: Page structure and findability
classes.rule: A docs or website page has a title unique per page and framework, headings in order, link text that names its target, and landmarks with unique names, and its help sits where it sits on every other page.

enforcedBy.note: a docs content pull request is never scanned

classes.name: Forms: redundant entry and drawn labels
classes.rule: A form keeps what the visitor typed when they switch tabs or steps, and a field has a drawn label, never a placeholder alone, that stays while they type.

classes.name: A screen reader's own behavior, not the grid's
Tool noise, documented behavior and missing goldens
